summary: Both are the same pattern — the whole strip, spatially uniform, breathing a single fixed-hue yellow up and down with an identical normalized envelope — but the port's hue sits ~7 degrees toward orange and its cycle runs ~11% fast (29.5 s vs 32.8 s).
observations: Structure: identical on both sides and trivially simple — every pixel of the 60 px strip holds the SAME colour at every instant. --dump at 11 times across a full cycle (labels dump-cycle, late) reports uniqColors=1 for all 60 pixels on both sides at every time. No bands, gradient, edges or spatial motion on either side; the waterfalls are pure horizontal banding.
Colour family: both sides are R>G, B=0 exactly at all times (meanB avg/min/max all 0 on both), i.e. a fully saturated yellow-to-orange hue with no blue channel and no palette walk.

Colour DIFFERENCE: the hue is constant through the whole cycle on both sides but differs between them. Original G/R = 0.898-0.905 at every sampled brightness (peak (255,229,0), mid (219,197,0), low (42,38,0), late-window (234,210,0)) -> hue ~= 0.150 (54 deg), a lemon yellow. Port G/R = 0.777-0.784 at every sampled brightness (peak (254,198,0), mid (226,176,0), low (10,8,0), late-window (241,188,0)) -> hue ~= 0.130 (47 deg), a golden/amber yellow. Visible side by side in the baseline waterfalls.

Brightness envelope SHAPE: identical. Resampling one full cycle to 32 phase points, normalized by each side's own peak, gives orig 1.000 0.994 0.963 0.919 0.851 0.776 0.689 0.596 0.497 0.404 0.304 0.224 0.143 0.081 0.037 0.006 0.000 ... and port 1.000 0.987 0.960 0.914 0.854 0.775 0.689 0.596 0.497 0.404 0.305 0.219 0.139 0.079 0.033 0.007 0.000 ... — a symmetric raised-cosine breath, matching within rounding at every phase. Both hold at exact black only briefly (orig 3.9% of frames at 0, port 3.8%) and both peak at full R=255.
Peak brightness: orig meanBrightness max 161, port 151. This gap is entirely the hue difference, not an envelope difference — both peak with R=255, the port just carries less green (G 198 vs 229).

TIMING DIFFERENCE (the main finding): the port's cycle is ~11% faster. Peak-to-peak and zero-to-zero measured on meanBrightness gives orig 32.78 s (peaks at 8.15 s / 40.90 s; zeros at 24.52 s / 57.30 s) and port 29.49 s (peaks at 7.33 s / 36.83 s / 66.30 s; zeros at 22.07 s / 51.55 s). Ratio orig/port = 1.111.

Phase offset is correct in normalized terms: both start t=0 at (132, G, 0) rising, and each side's first peak lands at 0.2487 of its own period, so the port is not phase-shifted — only its period is short. Consequence: the two drift steadily apart (by t=300 s they are ~10 s out of sync) with no re-sync.

Frame-rate coupling: NEITHER side is frame-rate coupled. Rendering both at 5, 10, 20 and 40 fps moved measured peak times by under 0.2 s (orig peak 8.00/8.10/8.15/8.18 s; port 7.20/7.25/7.33/7.35 s) — both are time-based, matching behaviour.

Steady state: both are healthy far out. A --skip 300 --seconds 70 window (label late) shows both still reaching their full peaks (orig max 161, port max 151) with the same periods (orig peaks 303.00/335.75/368.55 s; port 302.15/331.65/361.15 s). No decay, freeze, saturation or drift in amplitude on either side. The high zeroMotionFrames counts (orig 151, port 137 of 700) are the expected quantization effect of a very slow fade, not freezing.
Determinism: not random-driven. A --seed 7 run produced meanBrightness series byte-identical to --seed 1 on both sides, so no seed-dependent behaviour to judge.
feedback: Slow the fade cycle down by ~11%. The original's full dark->bright->dark period is 32.78 s; the port's is 29.49 s. Whatever sets the rate should be scaled by 32.78/29.49 = 1.111 (equivalently, the port is running at 0.90x the correct period). Verify by checking that consecutive meanBrightness peaks are 32.8 s apart, not 29.5 s.

Shift the hue slightly toward green. The original holds a constant green/red ratio of 0.898 (peak colour (255,229,0), hue ~0.150 or 54 deg); the port holds 0.780 (peak colour (254,198,0), hue ~0.130 or 47 deg). Target peak colour is (255,229,0) — the port currently reads as amber/gold where the original reads as lemon yellow. Nothing else about the colour needs touching: saturation (B=0) and the hue's constancy over the cycle are already exactly right.

Do NOT change anything else. Spatial behaviour (whole strip uniform, single colour everywhere), the raised-cosine breath envelope, the brief full-black bottom of the cycle, the starting phase (first peak at 0.249 of the period), full-red peak amplitude, time-based (fps-invariant) stepping, and the empty control surface all already match the original exactly.
